newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand pushes for orderly release of key data.
newsitem.headline: Thailand pushes for orderly release of key data.

text.p: BANGKOK, May 16 (Rueter) - Thai financial authorities will push for a more orderly release of key national economic data to avoid causing confusion among investors, the Bank of Thailand's deputy governor Chaiyawat Wibulswasdi said on Friday.
Chaiyawat chairs the Economic Information Committee, which was set up in February to coordinate economic data released by various national agencies.

Currently, agencies that release economic data include the Bank of Thailand, Finance Ministry, Commerce Ministry, Office of Agricultural Economics and Office of the National Economic and Social Development Board (NESBD).
"Presently, economic information is being disseminated by various government agencies, and in different formats," Chaiyawat said.

"Nevertheless, there still exists some misunderstanding and confusion when the data users do not receive a complete set of information, or the data released by different agencies differ depending on the respective purposes of data compilation," he added.

To enhance public understanding of official economic indicators, the committee on Friday issued a calendar for key macroecomic indicators, a summary of general characteristics of economic data, names of compiling and disseminating agencies and the release formats.

According to the calendar, the Bank of Thailand will continue to release key monthly economic data every last Thursday of the month, while other agencies will issue their data on a more regular basis.
The Finance Ministry's Customs Department, for example, will start releasing export and import data of the previous two months in the middle of every month.
The ministry will also release the country's fiscal position in the early part of each month.
Chaiwat said the trade figures released by various agencies may differ due to different methods of information gathering and objectives.
